title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-14
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, descending
ranking_explanation: The listed repositories are ordered by the daily gains displayed on GitHub Trending. Sponsor-marked cards and one repo with difficult-to-verify gaming-performance claims were excluded from this curated set. Total star counts, languages, default-branch names, and current commit SHAs were checked using GitHub REST.
global_caveat: Trending gains and total stars are live counts and may change after capture. This is a curated snapshot, not a complete census; sponsored entries and a repo with difficult-to-verify performance claims were omitted. No previous-window evidence was collected, so no notable-shift comparison is claimed.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-14 01:32 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-14 through 2026-11-14 (GitHub Trending: Today). Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, ranked descending; total stars and freshness checked against GitHub REST/Search APIs.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Coding-agent infrastructure dominates today’s strongest organic signals: Google’s modern-web guidance and OpenAI’s security workflow are attracting rapid attention, while several projects focus on keeping humans in the review loop. The top listed repository gained 1,925 stars today, far ahead of the rest of the curated set.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Source and evaluation toolkit for guidance that gives coding agents current web-platform practices.
sections.content: Source and evaluation toolkit for guidance that gives coding agents current web-platform practices. The README describes curated, token-efficient guidance and browser compatibility expertise intended to reduce legacy patterns in generated web code.
sections.why_notable: The largest daily gain in this curated snapshot; it packages browser expertise and compatibility guidance for agents rather than relying on generic model recall.
sections.unique_caveat: This -src repository is the source and evaluation project; the README points end users to the separate Modern Web Guidance package and documentation.

sections.title: we-promise/sure
sections.content: A community-maintained, self-hostable personal-finance application. The README describes browser, desktop, mobile, API, and agent access paths.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest gain; its README identifies it as a community fork of the archived Maybe Finance project, with multiple client and access paths.
sections.unique_caveat: The project is a community fork of the archived Maybe Finance application, not the original project.

sections.title: openai/codex-security
sections.description: Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing software vulnerabilities.
sections.content: Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing software vulnerabilities. Documented workflows cover scans, validating findings, patching, CI, integrations, and exports.
sections.why_notable: Strong security-agent momentum, with documented scan, finding-validation, patch, CI, and export workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The README notes that some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require Trusted Access for Cyber or another eligible access program.

sections.title: tailscale/tailcat
sections.description: A netcat-style utility over Tailscale’s encrypted data plane, without its control plane.
sections.content: A netcat-style utility over Tailscale’s encrypted data plane, without its control plane. Its README describes WireGuard-encrypted point-to-point tunnels and out-of-band exchange of connection metadata.
sections.why_notable: A networking counterpoint to the agent-heavy leaders; it uses Tailscale’s data plane while exchanging connection metadata out of band.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says connection metadata is exchanged out of band; users need a separate way to coordinate that metadata.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: An AI-assisted code-review tool combining deterministic checks with agent-based review.
sections.content: An AI-assisted code-review tool combining deterministic checks with agent-based review. The README describes reading diffs and broader file context, then producing structured line-level comments; it also supports whole-file scans.
sections.why_notable: Its stated differentiator is a hybrid of rules and LLM tool use, with structured line-level findings and support for configurable model endpoints.
sections.unique_caveat: The tool requires a configured model endpoint for LLM-assisted review.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A local browser-based review surface for plans, artifacts, agent messages, diffs, and pull requests.
sections.content: A local browser-based review surface for plans, artifacts, agent messages, diffs, and pull requests. It supports multiple coding agents and sends annotations and review feedback back into agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: Makes human feedback a first-class step across multiple coding agents, including annotations and review feedback returned to agent sessions.
sections.unique_caveat: The main review surface is local and browser-based; it is an integration layer rather than a standalone coding agent.

sections.title: block/buzz
sections.description: A self-hostable collaboration workspace where people and agents share rooms, workflows, and an event log.
sections.content: A self-hostable collaboration workspace where people and agents share rooms, workflows, and an event log. The README describes signed events, shared project rooms, workflow triggers, and agent identities with their own audit trail.
sections.why_notable: Extends agent collaboration beyond chat: its README describes shared project rooms, workflow triggers, and agent identities with their own audit trail.
sections.unique_caveat: The README distinguishes features that work today from mobile and workflow features still being wired up; its vision documents include ideas not yet implemented.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: A Claude Skills-based toolkit for structured market review, risk management, trade planning, and journaling.
sections.content: A Claude Skills-based toolkit for structured market review, risk management, trade planning, and journaling. The README explicitly frames it as decision-process support rather than an automated signal service.
sections.why_notable: A practical domain-specific agent workflow set; the author explicitly frames it as decision-process support, not an automated signal or promise of returns.
sections.unique_caveat: The README disclaims financial advice and automated trading; workflows may require external data or broker integrations for some features.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: Chrome DevTools exposed to coding agents through MCP and a CLI.
sections.content: Chrome DevTools exposed to coding agents through MCP and a CLI. It supports browser automation, debugging, network inspection, screenshots, and performance tracing.
sections.why_notable: Brings live-browser inspection, automation, debugging, and performance tracing into agent workflows; this established project is still receiving daily interest.
sections.unique_caveat: The README officially supports Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only and warns that the MCP client can inspect or modify browser data.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent guidance and security: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src supplies curated, token-efficient web-platform guidance; openai/codex-security applies agent workflows to vulnerability discovery and repair. Human-in-the-loop agent work: backnotprop/plannotator routes annotations and review feedback back to agents, while block/buzz treats agents as workspace participants with auditable identities. Agent developer tooling: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp exposes browser diagnostics and alibaba/open-code-review combines rules with LLM review. Self-hosting and control: we-promise/sure and block/buzz emphasize self-hosting; tailscale/tailcat avoids the Tailscale control plane. Languages: TypeScript 4/9, Go 2/9, and Ruby, Rust, Python one each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today’s strongest signal is not simply “more agents”; it is the tooling around agents—fresh domain guidance, security checks, browser access, and review interfaces that preserve human oversight. Outside that cluster, self-hostable finance and collaboration apps plus a focused private-network utility show that practical user-facing and infrastructure projects still break through.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily captured 2026-11-14 01:32 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository, README, and default-branch commit endpoints for all listed repos; Search API query stars:>1000 pushed:>2026-11-12 sorted by updated returned GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src, backnotprop/plannotator, and alibaba/open-code-review among the selected repositories. Daily gains came from GitHub Trending; total stars, languages, and commit SHAs from GitHub REST. Counts may change after capture. No notable-shift comparison was made.
